newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS near cargo deal with Lufthansa. [CORRECTED 16:46 GMT]
newsitem.headline: SAS near cargo deal with Lufthansa. [CORRECTED 16:46 GMT]

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) said on Tuesday that talks with Germany's Lufthansa on expanding an existing passenger alliance to cargo traffic were going well and would be completed next month.

"Our discussions with Lufthansa on a cargo cooperation deal are in their final stages. I expect a final deal to be signed within the next two to three weeks," SAS Cargo director Peter Groenlund told Reuters. (Corrects director's name.)
"Our talks are progressing in a constructive and positive manner," he said, adding that likely areas of cooperation were joint handling, sales and marketing.
SAS and Lufthansa formed a strategic alliance on passenger traffic in January 1996 and it was known that the two carriers were engaged in talks on a deal on cargo cooperation.

SAS is currently expanding its cargo activities. Earlier on Tuesday work began on building a new 500 million Danish crown SAS cargo terminal at Copenhagen International Airport and another new terminal is being built at Newark airport, New Jersey.
A third SAS cargo terminal is to be erected at Oslo's Gardermoen airport later this year, with all three terminals scheduled to be in operation by early 1999 at the latest.
All in all SAS' investment in new cargo facilities to cover expected freight demand for the next five to 10 years has amounted to one billion crowns, Groenlund said.
The new Copenhagen cargo terminal will be the hub of SAS Cargo's activities with annual capacity of 350,000 tonnes, he said.

In the first three quarters of 1996, SAS Cargo increased its total freight by over 20 percent compared to 1995's first nine months to 155,000 tonnes. --Soeren Linding Jakobsen, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
